result.topic_en: Gauss derives an addition relation for an integral of the lemniscatic type, showing that under the lemniscatic addition condition the sum of the integrals of x^2 dx/sqrt(1-x^4) equals d(xyz), and then states the resulting addition formula for the function F and for a modified function G.
result.transcription:
Aus $du = \frac{xxdx}{\sqrt{(1-x^4)}} + \frac{yydy}{\sqrt{(1-y^4)}} + \frac{zzdz}{\sqrt{(1-z^4)}}$
$0 = \frac{dx}{\sqrt{(1-x^4)}} + \frac{dy}{\sqrt{(1-y^4)}} + \frac{dz}{\sqrt{(1-z^4)}}$
folgt
$du = (yy-xx).\frac{dy}{\sqrt{(1-y^4)}} + (zz-xx).\frac{dz}{\sqrt{(1-z^4)}}$
$= xzdy + xydz [-+-] - yz.\sqrt{(1-x^4)}\left(\frac{dy}{\sqrt{(1-y^4)}} + \frac{dz}{\sqrt{(1-z^4)}}\right)$
$= xzdy + xydz + yzdx = d.\overline{xyz}$
Also
// $u = xyz$
Es ist folglich
$F(a+b) = Fa + Fb - \mathrm{sl}.a.\mathrm{sl}b.\mathrm{sl}(a+b)$
Setzt man
$Fa - \frac{a}{90^\circ}.F90^\circ = Ga$ so ist
$G(a+b) = Ga + Gb - \mathrm{sl}a\,\mathrm{sl}b\,\mathrm{sl}(a+b)$
$Ga = \frac{d\,Qa}{Qa}$

methods.what: Addition theorem for the lemniscatic integral of the second kind: under the condition dx/√(1-x^4)+dy/√(1-y^4)+dz/√(1-z^4)=0, the sum of the integrals of x^2dx/√(1-x^4) equals xyz
Addition formula for the function F (lemniscatic integral of the second kind) in terms of the lemniscatic sine
Subtracting the linear part gives a function G with the same addition formula, expressed as a logarithmic derivative of a function Q
